articles.title: I Built a Free Browser Shooter Set in a Pakistani Old-City Bazaar
articles.excerpt: I built a shooter set in a Pakistani bazaar, and it runs in a desktop browser. There is nothing to install. The game is called Operation Androon. A match is 8 v 8 team deathmatch against computer-cont…
articles.body: I built a shooter set in a Pakistani bazaar, and it runs in a desktop browser. There is nothing to install. The game is called Operation Androon. A match is 8 v 8 team deathmatch against computer-controlled soldiers, and the first team to 50 eliminations wins. The map is Purana Shehr: an old-city bazaar with a clock tower, shop signs in Urdu, decorated trucks, rickshaws, fruit stalls, and a haveli courtyard. I am a lead full-stack engineer in Lahore, and the founder of MyLeadBots. On my site, azeemshafeeq.com, I describe these games as side projects where I learn game development. Androon is one of them. This post is a clear look at what is in the game, what it needs, and what it is not. The place: Purana Shehr Purana Shehr is a fictional Pakistani old-city bazaar.
articles.author: M.Azeem

articles.title: Website Project Estimates: How to Compare Quotes Beyond the Headline
articles.excerpt: Website estimates are hard to compare when each proposal describes a different project. A useful comparison starts with scope and assumptions—not a single headline number. The goal is to understand wh…
articles.body: Website estimates are hard to compare when each proposal describes a different project. A useful comparison starts with scope and assumptions—not a single headline number. The goal is to understand what is included, what your team must provide, and what will continue to cost money after launch. List the deliverables before requesting quotes Describe the key user journeys, page types, languages, content migration, and systems the site must connect to. Note whether you need a content management system, custom workflows, user accounts, payment processing, or integrations with existing tools. Include who will write and approve content, supply images, and make decisions. These details can change the effort more than the number of pages alone.
articles.author: krishna kumar

articles.title: Every URL in our sitemap says 3 October, and 30 of the 76 pages changed after that
articles.excerpt: Here is a check you can run on our site in one command: curl -s https://nakodo.app/sitemap.xml | grep -o ' [^ 2026-10-03. All 76 URLs, one date, forty-one days ago. Now open our privacy notice. Under…
articles.body: Here is a check you can run on our site in one command: curl -s https://nakodo.app/sitemap.xml | grep -o '<lastmod>[^<]*' | sort -u One line comes back. <lastmod>2026-10-03 . All 76 URLs, one date, forty-one days ago. Now open our privacy notice . Under the heading it says Last updated 28 October 2026 . The same deployment is telling a human one date and a crawler another, about the same URL, and the gap is twenty-five days. I went looking for how many of the 76 are in that position. The answer is 30. Where the date comes from Nakodo is an app that finds creators for a brand and emails the ones that fit. Its public side is 76 pages, and all 76 are rows in one registry, which is the arrangement I have written about before: sixty-three of our pages are one component .

articles.title: Obfuscating a .NET AWS Lambda Function Without Breaking the Handler String
articles.excerpt: A .NET AWS Lambda function is close to the ideal obfuscation target. It is a small class library — no Main in the managed case, no UI, one method that Lambda calls — that ships to infrastructure you d…
articles.body: A .NET AWS Lambda function is close to the ideal obfuscation target. It is a small class library — no Main in the managed case, no UI, one method that Lambda calls — that ships to infrastructure you do not administer and runs headless. Almost nothing in it is consumed by name from outside. And yet, like other serverless shapes, it hides one seam where a naive obfuscation pass produces a failure that looks nothing like an obfuscation bug: the package deploys, the assembly loads, and the very first invocation fails with a handler-resolution error, long before any of your code runs. The DLL is valid. Lambda simply cannot find the one method it was told to call.
articles.author: Zero Heartbeat

articles.title: Designing Scalable APIs: 10 Things Most Developers Miss
articles.excerpt: Building a REST API is relatively straightforward. You define routes, create controllers, validate requests, interact with a database and return JSON responses. But designing an API that remains relia…
articles.body: Building a REST API is relatively straightforward. You define routes, create controllers, validate requests, interact with a database and return JSON responses. But designing an API that remains reliable as the application grows is a different challenge. An API that works perfectly with 100 records might struggle with 100,000 records. An endpoint that works under normal network conditions might create duplicate transactions when clients retry failed requests. The difference between an API that works and one that is production-ready often comes down to decisions made during its design. In this article, I'll explore 10 important considerations developers should think about when building scalable APIs, using Laravel and PHP examples where appropriate. 1.

articles.body: The self-styled visionaries of Silicon Valley, leaders like OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, have built careers claiming to see the future. Long-term vision is currency: Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg built a 10-year road map for Facebook in 2016, and Google famously told investors before its public offering that it was unconcerned with short-term results. And yet there they all were, a mere five weeks before the midterm elections, gathered at the White House to smile for photos with President Trump and sign on to his “Super Intelligence” agenda. Even by the diminished standards of today’s corporate governance, this was a shockingly foolish decision.
